events.headline: Caleb Williams unlikely to play Monday vs. Eagles, per Rapoport; Case Keenum set to start
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 24 item. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports Williams is unlikely to play Monday night against Philadelphia with the hamstring strain he suffered on a fourth-quarter scramble against Minnesota (MRI showed no tear). Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol after a hit from Andrew Van Ginkel, and both were non-participants Thursday, so 38-year-old Case Keenum is in line for his first regular-season start since 2023. Kyle Monangai (knee) and kicker Cairo Santos (right hip) were also Thursday non-participants. Hamstrings like Williams's typically cost two to four weeks.
events.so_what: Plan the Monday game around Keenum rather than hoping for a late Williams surprise, and treat every Bears pass catcher as a downgrade. Monangai's knee still matters: if he sits, D'Andre Swift's share of the backfield grows. Santos's hip keeps the Bears kicker in doubt, and a kicker who might not dress can't be trusted to score by the distance bands.

He was hurt five plays into the opener against New England, and the initial timeline ran from a couple of weeks to over a month.

events.headline: Jaxson Dart undergoes season-ending knee surgery; Jameis Winston is the Giants starter
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. Dart had season-ending surgery Wednesday and the Giants formally placed him on injured reserve Thursday; the damage includes the MCL, PCL and meniscus, with no ACL involvement. Jameis Winston was already named the starter going forward, beginning Week 3 at home against Tennessee. Malik Nabers' right shoulder popped out in the same Monday night loss to the Rams; he popped it back in and returned, and no further diagnosis has been reported. On Wednesday the Giants listed Nabers as limited with the shoulder (an estimated report, since they held a walkthrough), with no quotes on his status.
events.so_what: No longer a planning question: Dart is done for 2026 and the Giants' rushing-QB premium goes with him. Winston throws more and riskier balls, which can mean more volume for Nabers and the other pass catchers alongside more drive-ending interceptions (only a point each here). Nabers being limited rather than out on the first report is a mild positive; watch Friday's designation before locking him in.

events.detail: Update to the Sept. 23 item. Flowers (hamstring) sat out Thursday for the second straight day and has not practiced in any form since Friday of last week. The Ravens fly to Brazil overnight for Sunday's game against Dallas and were set to announce the travel party later Thursday. Ronnie Stanley (toe) also sat. events.headline: Falcons rout Packers 35-14 on TNF: Penix active and efficient, Bijan runs for 194, Packers' backfield manages 17 yards
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. Michael Penix Jr. was active after a full practice and went 18 of 25 for 256 yards, a touchdown and an interception in his first start back from the ACL. Atlanta ran for 244 yards: Bijan Robinson had 194 and a touchdown, Brian Robinson Jr. added a score, and Drake London caught 9 passes for 194 yards. Green Bay ran only nine times for 17 yards, with MarShawn Lloyd (4-11) and Kaleb Johnson (4-6) splitting the carries; Josh Jacobs remains on the commissioner exempt list and Jayden Reed was out. Jordan Love threw 52 times for 312 yards and two touchdowns.
events.so_what: Penix running an offense this efficiently keeps Bijan and London at the top of their positions rather than capped behind a struggling quarterback. The Packers have no running game: neither Lloyd nor Kaleb Johnson is a start while the carries are split this way at this volume, and a Love who throws 52 times is a volume play, not a fade.
